title: Cider Pond: autumn ducks, falling leaves and a looping miniature camera
author: loktar00
prompt: Create one complete, self-contained HTML file for CIDER POND, a bright October afternoon on a small forest lake where a mallard family paddles among falling leaves, as a self-running three.js scene with no interaction.  Use a warm, painterly autumn aesthetic: pale sky-reflecting water as the brightest surface in frame; scarlet and red maples, gold birches and aspens, rust and copper oaks, all deciduous, with not a single pine, conifer or evergreen anywhere; muted olive reeds and lily pads; warm brown trunks and dock timber, never black; a thin matching haze; and a tilt-shift miniature look applied as a post-process pass over the final frame: a strong depth-of-field blur across the top and bottom of the frame with a sharp horizontal band of focus through the pond, and slightly boosted saturation and contrast, so the whole scene reads like a toy diorama. The result should feel like a sunlit storybook painting while still being a smooth, detailed real-time scene. Do not make it dark, crushed, noisy or visibly low-poly, and never a stained-glass look.  Include a large still lake ringed by natural deciduous trees with visible trunks and real branching, each crown an irregular layered mass of clustered autumn colour rather than a single sphere or cone on a stick, varied in height, some half-bare; a mallard hen leading a line of ducklings, several drakes with green heads and white neck rings, and one white farm duck, all leaving V-shaped wakes that spread and fade; ducks that paddle in smooth arcs toward wandering waypoints, tip tail-up to dabble, preen on a rock or the dock, splash gently if they bump, and never leave the water; cattails and reeds along the edges, lily pads in the shallows, a small wooden dock with a footbridge, a mossy log, a short stone path with a bench, and mushrooms at the tree roots; a heron standing in the shallows; dragonflies skimming the reeds; and leaves falling, spiralling down, settling on the water, drifting in rafts and pushed aside as a duck passes. Build every tree, bird and plant from geometry and materials in code; never hotlink a model or an image. Reflect the coloured trees softly on the water, broken by the leaves and the wakes. Make it fill the window, resize cleanly, hold 60 fps and start with zero console errors. Deliver it as a single self-contained HTML file; any libraries are allowed.

title: <inputs> Ask me for: a voiceover or song with a spoken line (the…
author: twoclipping
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a voiceover or song with a spoken line (the audio file) and its transcript, 10-12 small objects that sum up my life, two silhouettes to light like a heat camera (a head in profile and a raised hand), and the 3 words I want to land hardest. If I skip any, use the defaults: vinyl, book, camera, cat, coin, game controller, cap, heart, money, plant, clapperboard, skateboard; free CC0 silhouettes from Openverse; action, intention, curiosity.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 20 second 4:3 film, 1440x1080 at 60fps, cut to the voice. Off-white paper, black, one red, one yellow, Geist for every word. Film grain on everything, a soft vignette, and a camera that never rests: a slow handheld float under everything plus a slow push inside every scene.
No scene cuts to the next: each handoff starts on the exact last frame of the scene before. The only hard cuts are the beat flips on the last word.
Every object is pixel art you draw yourself: a 16x16 grid per object, every cell a hand-placed colour, rendered as a 3D block (a darker extrusion down-right, a thin bevel on every cell) with a soft contact shadow.
The silhouettes are lit like a heat camera: the heat comes from how thick the body is at each point, so the nose, the hair and the fingertips run cooler, plus one hotspot and a slow moving noise, mapped through a black > red > orange > cream ramp. The edge stays razor sharp, with a soft glow outside it.
Motion rules: nothing pops in (eased glides of about 0.5s with a soft start), fast moves get real motion blur instead of ghost copies, and captions type with the voice behind a block cursor.
Banned: stock footage, AI video, 3D camera moves, particles, glitch.
</direction>

<structure>
Hang every scene on the transcript's word timings (measure them with faster-whisper word timestamps, one short chunk at a time):
1. The first word fills a yellow card. The card wipes off to the left and the question types underneath on two centred lines that glide to stay centred as they grow, the key word underlined in red as it's spoken.
2. The objects streak past in lanes above and below the words, a cyan four-point flare sweeps in, then the page burns away: black closes in from the edges onto the head, behind a hot red edge.
3. The head heats up on black while the answer types low on the left. A thin white orbit draws itself around the head, its far half passing behind it. On the last word, paper blooms out from inside the head with the objects in it, and the camera falls through: the head rushes past the lens until the paper is all we see.
4. The objects sit on a tilted ring seen in perspective (the front ones bigger and lower, drawn last), slowly turning, each one bobbing; the coin flips and lands with sparks.
5. On each of the 3 words, that object flies out of the ring to the left and grows, the page floods black from it, and the word types beside it (camera: a red shutter star; book: a red ribbon sweep; record: two white orbits and red notes). Then the flood drains back into the object as it flies home, and the camera dives closer into the ring. Put each hero object in the slot that is front-left when its word lands.
6. The ring pulls in a touch, bursts outward, every object turns to ink, and ink blots grow and swallow the page.
7. The hand rises into frame, hot, with the line split either side of it. The heart drops into its palm, then lifts to the centre at the size the next scene holds it.
8. The last word, one letter per beat, the background flipping paper / black / red, the heart holding its place across the cut, the centre object morphing pixel by pixel into the next one.
9. Thin brush strokes sweep through, the letters drift apart and float, then settle back into the word with the heart above it. The camera keeps pushing through the hold.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas. Every frame is a pure function of time inside seek(t).
2. Bake each pixel sprite once to an offscreen canvas (the extrusion layers, then the face), then draw it scaled and rotated.
3. The heat: precompute each silhouette's base heat once (a distance transform of the mask, held at the edge value outside it so nothing dark bleeds in when it is upscaled). Every frame, add the hotspot and two octaves of value noise at quarter resolution, map it through a 256-step lookup, upscale it, and cut it with the full-resolution mask.
4. The fall through the head: draw the ring scene into an offscreen layer, mask it with the head scaled up about a point inside the skull, and grow that scale on a cubed curve until the head covers the frame. The ring inside zooms less than the head does, so it reads as depth.
5. The pixel morph: pair every cell of object A with a cell of object B and glide each one's position and colour, with a small random delay per cell.
6. Render with Playwright at 60fps with 8 motion-blur subframes, then lay the original audio back on with ffmpeg.
</build>

<gotchas>
A mask PNG with no alpha channel fills the whole box with heat, so put the silhouette in the alpha. A limb cut by the photo's border shows as a straight edge, so extend the mask past the frame. A handoff only reads as smooth when the last frame of one scene is the first frame of the next: draw the outgoing scene under the transition, and give scenes that show the same ring one shared zoom function. A flood that's still retreating when the next scene starts reads as a hard cut, so let it finish first. A fast ease-out flood reads as a jump; use a soft start.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, measure the word timings, then show me 8 stills before you render.
</start>

title: <inputs> Ask me for: my product's name (nightshift) (one lowercase…

<direction>

Nothing cuts: every scene grows out of the last, shapes morph, dots fly, colours change under floods. Every morph glides 0.8s on cubic-bezier(.45,0,.15,1) and the camera zoom rides the same curve. Geist, the real macOS pointer, soft shadows that grow with each shape's height.
Banned: flat or gradient backgrounds made in code, camera zooms into tiny points, hard cuts, crossfades between scenes, bouncy springs, particles, glows, holds longer than 1s, cropped type.
</direction>

<structure>
Beats are the song's. The song enters on its big hit as the first pill appears.
Open: the letters slide into the period and vanish into it while it glides to the middle. The period opens like an iris onto the night inside it, and "you log off at 6", then "[product] doesn't", roll through one mask line over the night photo.

Night: the composer becomes a glass orb with a progress ring. A clock chip swaps 11:42 PM, 3:17 AM, 5:02 AM, 6:59 AM while the sky relights from night to dawn and "while you sleep" rolls in.
Results (beat 20): the orb turns black and goo-splits into the three result pills. The checks pop green.
Morning: the pills merge into a Dynamic Island that grows into a phone lock screen: the day photo, the date, a big 7:00, the bezel growing out of the screen edge. Three glass notifications stack in, and the cursor taps the first, which opens like iOS.
Proof: a week calendar (10 meetings pop in, a hover shows one's time), then a pipeline chart ($48,200 counts up, the line draws, a hover follows it). A black flood from the line's end becomes "Start your night shift →" and the cursor clicks it.
Out: the button shrinks into a dot, the whole scene closes down into it like an iris, and the letters slide back out of the period. The tagline rises. Last frame = first frame.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas. Everything is a pure function of time inside seek(t): no timers, no state between frames.
2. One element morphs through every state (size, radius, colour, material) from a table of beat times, so retiming is one edit.
3. Render the inside world into an offscreen canvas and reveal it through the period with a circular mask. Never zoom the camera into the dot.
4. Glass: a pre-blurred copy of the photo clipped to the shape, then a tint and a gradient rim.
5. Goo: blur + alpha threshold on an offscreen layer for the split and the merge.
6. Sound: a downloaded SFX for every event, each placed by its measured peak. The song enters on its hit. Loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
7. Render with Playwright at 60fps with 4 motion-blur subframes. Scan every frame for single-frame jumps and fix each one.
</build>

<gotchas>
A camera zoom into an off-centre dot swings sideways and spikes, so open the dot instead. Ease a closing iris by area, not radius, or its first frames jump. A helper that sets globalAlpha must restore the caller's, or fading cards pop. Counters read the frame's time, not the subframe's, or the digits smear.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the beat map and 6 stills (open, find, write, results, phone, out) before you render.
</start>

title: Pixel art winter hockey scene comparison
author: N1njaCodex
prompt:
Build a real-time pixel-art isometric diorama of hockey on a frozen river, as a single HTML page using three.js (WebGL). A floating winter island: a frozen river crosses it from edge to edge and spills off both ends as icicle falls. On the black ice, a rink has been shovelled out and walled with a ring of snow lumps, with a gap for the bench and a small red-framed net with white mesh at each end. The nets are set in from the walls so players can go behind them. The north bank climbs to a terrace with snow-roofed log houses (smoking chimneys, icicles on the eaves, lit windows), a fence, birches with crows and a sledging slope. The south shore is low: firs, a snowman, a fire and a small bath-house. Add a footbridge upstream and an ice fisherman on a box over his hole downstream. Play three skaters and a goalie a side, village rules: no lines, no offside. The goalies wear felt boots and pads. Skaters have momentum: pushes to accelerate, long glides, limited turning, and hockey stops with a spray of snow. They skate backwards when defending and fall and slide on their backs after collisions. Simulate the puck physically: low friction on ice and high on snow, solved passes (v0² = v² + 2ad), saucer passes over sticks, lifted shots aimed through a spot in the net, soft snow walls that can bury a hard puck, posts and crossbar.
AI: a chaser chosen by intercept time, attack and defence shapes, a presser and markers, poke checks, dekes, wristers, snapshots, slapshots, backhands, wraparounds and one-timers, plus blocked shots. Goalies read the shot from a forecast, drop into the butterfly, stretch, glove or kick out rebounds, and cover the puck.
An old man drops the puck at faceoffs, catches the puck the beaten goalie slides up to him, and tosses spares when a puck is lost in the snow. A dog digs the lost pucks out and brings them back.
The rink is a live canvas: skate blades scratch it white, falling snow settles on it and slows the puck, kids clear lanes with snow scoops, and between games the old man floods it from buckets into a mirror.
Village life: sledders, the fisherman catching perch, a woman crossing the bridge with a yoke of buckets, fans on a bench who comment, a boy on the snow wall who throws snowballs on click, crows, chimney smoke, breath in the frost. Day/dusk/night lighting with lamps, a string of bulbs and the fire; clear/snow/blizzard weather.
UI: a scoreboard, a side rail with team ladders, called moves, weather, snow on the ice and spare pucks, and a live feed. Original characters only, English UI, responsive down to phone width.

title: Code-based UI motion design loop
author: 0xAiky
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: 8 to 12 UI states I want the shape to transform into (e.g. button, loader, player, slider, toggle, tabs, chart, command palette, toast), pure black and white or one accent color, and a royalty-free song around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Dribbble-level UI motion. One shape, no cuts: every state is the same element morphing its size, radius and color while its content swaps with a quick blur.
A cursor controls every change with real clicks and drags. Light warm-gray canvas, black and white components, one clean UI font (Geist).
Springs everywhere, with only a tiny overshoot. The camera zooms so each state fills the entire frame. The last frame matches the first frame, so it loops perfectly.
Banned: bouncy easing, particle bursts, glows, gradients on UI chrome, mismatched icon strokes, dead time, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 7 bars, something happens on every beat.
Button → loader → check → dynamic island → music player with a play/pause morph → scrub the progress bar → it becomes a volume slider that stretches when dragged past max → a toggle flips on the beat → the knob becomes a liquid tab indicator → the tabs expand into a chart that draws itself, with a tooltip on hover → it collapses into ⌘K → type to filter → enter → toast → back to the button.
</structure>

<build>
One HTML file, square 1440x1440. Every style is calculated from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state carried between frames.
Springs use closed-form step responses. A value that changes targets multiple times is the sum of one spring per change, so it remains a pure function of time.
The tab indicator's two edges follow different springs, so the leading edge stretches ahead of the trailing one. Use the same trick for the toggle knob.
Drags use direct manipulation: while the cursor is held, the value is calculated from its position. On release it springs back from wherever it was.
Analyze the song with numpy to find the beat grid and start on a downbeat. Position every UI sound by its measured peak.
Render with Playwright: 4 subframes per frame, blended with ffmpeg tmix for motion blur at 60fps.
Render one frame per beat before the full render. Fix anything off the grid, cramped or difficult to read.
</build>

<gotchas>
Never put will-change on anything the camera scales or the text becomes blurry.
Text that swaps inside a morphing container needs its own enter and exit timing or it overlaps.
Make the final frame identical to the first, including cursor position and speed, or the loop stutters.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the state list on the beat grid before writing any code.
</start>

border-radius:0 20px 20px 0 } /* white "D" half-circle */ .logo b { font-weight:700 } .logo span { font-weight:400 } .nav-links { display:flex; gap:clamp(20px,4.1vw,60px); list-style:none } .nav-links a { color:#fff; text-decoration:none; font-size:15px; font-weight:500; position:relative } .nav-links a::after { content:''; position:absolute; left:0; right:0; bottom:-4px; height:1px; background:currentColor; transform:scaleX(0); transform-origin:right; transition:transform .35s ease } .nav-links a:hover::after { transform:scaleX(1); transform-origin:left } ARROWS (top-right, left of the dots column) .arrows { position:absolute; top:18.9%; left:76.7%; display:flex; gap:32px; transform:translate(-19px,-50%) } .arrow { width:38px; height:38px; border-radius:50%; border:2.5px solid #fff; background:transparent; color:#fff; display:grid; left:45.6%; right:-1vw; top:88.7%; transform:translateY(-50%); display:flex; align-items:center } .cta { flex:none; padding:0 15px; height:48px; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; border:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,.85); border-radius:6px; background:rgba(0,0,0,.15); color:#fff; font-size:14px; font-weight:400; text-decoration:none; cursor:pointer; transition:background .25s, color .25s } .cta:hover { background:#fff; color:#000 } .cta-line { flex:1; height:1.5px; background:rgba(255,255,255,.8); min-width:40px } .count { flex:none; font-size:clamp(140px,19.8vw,360px); font-weight:400; line-height:1; letter-spacing:-0.02em; color:transparent; -webkit-text-stroke:1.5px rgba(255,255,255,.9); transform:translateY(6%); user-select:none } LOADER .loader { position:absolute; left:50%; top:50%; transform:translate(-50%,-50%); font-size:12px; letter-spacing:.2em; text-transform:uppercase; opacity:.6; transition:opacity .6s } .loader.done { opacity:0 } RESPONSIVE @media (max-width:900px), (max-aspect-ratio:1/1) { .arrows { left:auto; right:var(--pad-x); top:15%; transform:translateY(-50%); gap:14px } .tagline { bottom:clamp(150px,20vh,220px) } .cta-row { left:var(--pad-x); right:-3vw; top:auto; bottom:24px; transform:none } .count { font-size:clamp(120px,22vw,200px) } } @media (max-width:640px) { .nav-links { gap:16px } .nav-links a, .logo { font-size:13px } .dots { gap:20px; right:16px } .dot { width:10px; height:10px } .cta-row { right:-8vw } .count { font-size:120px } } @media (max-width:420px) { .nav-links li:nth-child(2) { display:none } } /* hide "Portfolio" */ No horizontal page scroll at any width. ================================================== 4. WEBGL SCENE (Three.js) ================================================== Renderer: WebGLRenderer({ canvas:#scene, antialias:true, alpha:false }), clearColor #000, outputColorSpace SRGBColorSpace, pixelRatio = min(devicePixelRatio, 2). Camera: PerspectiveCamera(fov 30, aspect W/H, 0.1, 100) at (0,0,10) looking at origin. 4a. Background headline (drawn into an offscreen 2D canvas → CanvasTexture) - Canvas size = viewport × DPR, filled #000. - mobile = (W < 768) || (W/H < 1). - fontSize fs = min(H*0.21, W*(mobile ? 0.21 : 0.118)); font = `800 ${fs}px Poppins`. If the widest line is wider than W*(mobile ? 0.9 : 0.5), scale fs down to fit. - Lines: "Explore", "New", "Ideas". Fill #e9e9e9, textAlign center, baseline alphabetic. - Centre x = W*(mobile ? 0.5 : 0.505); centre y = H*(mobile ? 0.45 : 0.468). Line gap = fs*1.07; cap height ≈ fs*0.7. Line i (0..2) baseline y = cy + cap/2 + (i-1)*gap. - Texture: colorSpace SRGB, LinearFilter, no mipmaps. Redraw on resize and on document.fonts 'loadingdone'. - Show it with a fullscreen quad (PlaneGeometry(2,2), ShaderMaterial, vertex outputs position.xy directly, fragment = texture2D(uTex, vUv) followed by #include <colorspace_fragment> ON ITS OWN LINE; depthTest/depthWrite false; frustumCulled false) in its own bgScene. - Wait for fonts before first draw: Promise.race([Promise.all([document.fonts.load('800 100px Poppins'), document.fonts.ready]), 2500ms timeout]) then layout() + start loop. 4b. Model loading - GLTFLoader.load(MODEL_URL). Traverse gltf.scene; for each mesh: clone geometry, delete 'uv','color','tangent' attributes, mergeVertices(g, 1e-4), computeVertexNormals(), applyMatrix4(mesh.matrixWorld). Merge all parts with mergeGeometries. - Centre the geometry on its bounding box and scale uniformly so its largest dimension = 1. - Scene graph: scene → pivot (screen position + scale) → spinner (rotation) → cube mesh. On load add class "done" to #loader. 4c. Cube placement (in layout(), on load and on resize) - visH = 2*tan(fov/2)*10; visW = visH*aspect. - Screen-fraction centre: sx = mobile ? 0.5 : 0.517, sy = mobile ? 0.45 : 0.488. pivot.position = ((sx-0.5)*visW, (0.5-sy)*visH, 0). - On-screen edge length px = min(H*0.44, W*(mobile ? 0.45 : 0.29)); pivot.scale = (px/H)*visH. - Initial spinner rotation: Euler(-0.42, 0.62, 0.18). 4d. Glass material — custom ShaderMaterial, screen-space refraction with 6-band chromatic dispersion, rendered in two passes (back faces, then front faces). Vertex shader: varying vec3 vNormal; varying vec3 vEye; worldPos = modelMatrix*position; mvPos = viewMatrix*worldPos; gl_Position = projectionMatrix*mvPos; vNormal = normalize(normalMatrix*normal); vEye = normalize(https://mvpos.xyz/); Fragment shader: uv = gl_FragCoord.xy / uResolution (drawing-buffer size). n = normalize(vNormal); if (uBackside > 0.5) n = -n; // do NOT use gl_FrontFacing, three.js flips winding for BackSide eye = normalize(vEye). LOOP = 16 iterations; slide = i/LOOP * 0.045. For each band compute refract(eye, n, 1.0/ior) with iorR/Y/G/C/B/P and sample uTexture at uv + refr.xy * (uRefractPower + slide*k) * uChromatic, with k = 1 (R), 1 (Y), 2 (G), 2.5 (C), 3 (B), 1 (P): r = tex(R).x*0.5 y = (tex(Y).x*2 + tex(Y).y*2 - tex(Y).z)/6 g = tex(G).y*0.5 c = (tex(C).y*2 + tex(C).z*2 - tex(C).x)/6 b = tex(B).z*0.5 p = (tex(P).z*2 + tex(P).x*2 - tex(P).y)/6 R = r + (2p + 2y - c)/3; G = g + (2y + 2c - p)/3; B = b + (2c + 2p - y)/3 color += vec3(R,G,B) color /= LOOP; saturation adjust: mix(luma(color), color, uSaturation) with luma weights (0.2125, 0.7154, 0.0721). Specular (Blinn-Phong, light vector = normalize(-light), view = -eye): spec = specular(uLight, uShininess, uDiffuseness) + 0.6 * specular(vec3(1,1,-1), uShininess*0.6, uDiffuseness*0.5) spec(x) = pow(max(dot(n,halfVec),0), shininess) + max(0,dot(n,lightVec))*diffuseness color += spec * (backside ? 0.35 : 1.0) Fresnel: f = pow(1.0 + dot(eye, n), uFresnelPower); color = mix(color, vec3(1), f * (backside ? 0.25 : 0.55)). color += vec3(0.004, 0.005, 0.007). gl_FragColor = vec4(color,1); then #include <colorspace_fragment> on its own line. Uniform values: uIorR 1.15, uIorY 1.16, uIorG 1.18, uIorC 1.22, uIorB 1.22, uIorP 1.22, uRefractPower 0.30 (front) / 0.22 (back), uChromatic 0.5, uSaturation 1.08, uShininess 90, uDiffuseness 0.02, uFresnelPower 5.0, uLight (-1, 1, 1), uBackside 0 (frontMat, side FrontSide) / 1 (backMat, side BackSide). 4e. Render pipeline (every frame) - Two WebGLRenderTargets sized to drawing buffer (W*DPR × H*DPR), type HalfFloatType, default (linear) colour space: rtBack, rtFront. - backMat.uTexture = rtBack.texture; frontMat.uTexture = rtFront.texture. 1) render bgScene → rtBack 2) render bgScene → rtFront, then (autoClear=false) cube with backMat → rtFront 3) render bgScene → screen, then (autoClear=false, clearDepth) cube with frontMat → screen - This gives the look: text seen through the cube is magnified, mirrored and split into blue/yellow fringes, inner rounded edges of the cube are faintly visible, and the bevelled edges glow white. ================================================== 5. INTERACTION & ANIMATION ================================================== - Drag to rotate (pointer events on the canvas, setPointerCapture): dx = Δx*0.008, dy = Δy*0.008; apply as world-space rotation: premultiply spinner.quaternion by axisAngle(Y, dx) then axisAngle(X, dy). Track velocity per 16.67ms frame; add class "dragging" to the canvas while dragging. - Inertia after release: keep applying velocity, damped by 0.94^(dt*60) per frame. - Idle drift: 0.6s after release, blend in a constant slow rotation of 0.0035 rad/frame around Y and 0.0012 rad/frame around X (blend ramps 0→1 over 1s). It also runs from page load. - Prev/Next arrow buttons: smoothly rotate the cube -90°/+90° around Y (ease: each frame apply remaining*min(1, 0.09*dt*60) until remaining < 0.0005). Cancels inertia; dragging cancels the spin. - Dots: clicking a dot makes it the only .active one (hollow ring). - Hover transitions: nav link underline wipe (.35s), arrow and CTA buttons invert to white bg / black content (.25s). - Clamp frame dt to 0.05s. Recompute layout (renderer size, camera aspect, render-target sizes, uResolution, headline canvas, cube position/scale) on window resize. ================================================== 6. LAYOUT REFERENCE (desktop 1440×806) ================================================== - Logo at (100, 38), 40px tall. Nav links right-aligned, right edge ≈ 1340, vertical centre ≈ 58. - Arrow circles centred at ≈ (1105, 152) and (1175, 152). - Dots at x ≈ 1340, y ≈ 351 / 398 / 445 (middle one hollow). - Headline "Explore / New / Ideas" centred at x ≈ 727, ~170px ExtraBold, baselines ≈ 272 / 445 / 637. - Glass cube occupies ≈ x 510–1000, y 145–600, slightly right of centre, overlapping the headline. - Tagline "Let's Build the / Future of / Design." at left 100, bottom ≈ 60px, ~38px, Light with Bold "Design.". - "Explore Now" button at (657, 691), 48px tall; a 1.5px line runs right to a huge outlined "07" whose "0" starts at x ≈ 1140 and whose "7" is clipped by the right and bottom edges. - Pure black background, all UI white. Mobile (≤767px or portrait): headline and cube centred at 50% x / 45% y, headline up to 90% width, arrows move under the nav on the right, tagline sits above the CTA row, and the CTA row is pinned 24px from the bottom with "07" partly off-screen on the right. Output: one complete index.html, nothing else.

title: Explainer video of 9 football rules
author: lukasersil
prompt:
Postav mi video, které vysvětluje pravidla sportu stylem televizní analýzy s AR grafikou. Bez AI video modelů a bez stahování assetů: 3D scénu, postavy, textury, grafiku i zvuk vytvoř kódem. Pracuj samostatně a průběžně mi ukazuj kontrolní snímky.

## Parametry (pro jiný sport změň tuhle sekci a sekci Scénář)
- Sport: fotbal
- Pravidla (9): ofsajd, faul, pokutový kop, vhazování, rohový kop + kop od branky, hra rukou, přímý volný kop, žlutá a červená karta, gól (celý míč za čarou)
- Jazyk všech textů: čeština (plná diakritika, desetinná čárka)
- Délka: cca 68 s (úvod ~4,5 s, každé pravidlo 6 až 8 s, závěr ~4 s)
- Formát: 1920×1080, 30 fps, MP4 (H.264 + AAC)
- Styl postav: PS2 éra ve stylu GTA San Andreas (low-poly tvarované tělo, ručně malované textury)
- Týmy: Červení (červený dres s bílými lemy, bílé trenky), Modří (královsky modrý dres, tmavě modré trenky), rozhodčí černý s limetkovými lemy, brankáři zelený a fialový

## Technologie a pipeline
- Three.js (npm). index.html obsahuje WebGL canvas 1920×1080 a nad ním DOM vrstvu pro HUD.
- Deterministická funkce `window.renderFrame(t)`: stav scény i HUD je čistá funkce času, žádný stav mezi snímky.
- `render.mjs`: lokální statický HTTP server + puppeteer-core se systémovým Chrome (headless, na Macu `--use-angle=metal`). Pro každý snímek zavolej renderFrame(t), počkej 2× requestAnimationFrame, udělej JPEG screenshot a pošli ho rourou do ffmpeg (libx264, CRF 18, yuv420p). Režimy: `stills t1 t2 …` (PNG na kontrolu), `video`, `info` (zapíše časovou osu do out/timeline.json).
- Cesty řeš přes fileURLToPath (složky s mezerami v názvu).
- WebGLRenderer s `preserveDrawingBuffer: true`, ACES tone mapping, PCF soft shadows. EffectComposer s MSAA (samples 4, HalfFloat): RenderPass, UnrealBloomPass, vlastní grade pass (vinětace, jemné zrno, chromatická aberace, záblesk, whip blur, VHS efekt), OutputPass.
- Zvuk: Python (numpy + scipy) syntetizuje celý soundtrack do WAV, ffmpeg ho přimíchá (AAC 192k).
- Výstupy: plná kvalita + webová verze (CRF 23 až 24, maxrate 10M).

## Struktura projektu
src/util.js (easing, tmap pro freeze a zpomalení, track() pro pohyb hráčů po časovaných waypointech s fází běhu podle uražené vzdálenosti, seeded rng), src/world.js, src/player.js, src/ar.js, src/hud.js, src/grade.js, src/segments.js, src/main.js, render.mjs, https://audio.py/, PROGRESS.md (průběžně zapisuj, co je hotové a jak se to pouští, ať se dá navázat po přerušení).

## Svět
- Hřiště 105×68 m. Tráva jako canvas textura (pruhy po 5,25 m, šum, skvrny) + dlaždicová detail textura přes onBeforeCompile. Čáry jako ostrá geometrie, ne textura. Vnější hrana čar = hranice hřiště.
- Branky se sítí (LineSegments), rohové praporky.
- Stadion: dvoupatrová mísa podle superelipsy, dav jako canvas textura lidí v řadách, LED pás mezi patry, střecha s žebry, řady reflektorů na hraně střechy (emisivní, bloom), vnější fasáda s osvětlenými okny, noční obloha, světla města kolem, tmavá zem.
- LED mantinely kolem hřiště s českými nápisy (PRAVIDLA FOTBALU, RESPEKT, FAIR PLAY, ZNEJ PRAVIDLA, #PRAVIDLAFOTBALU), pomalu se posouvají.
- Světla: 4 směrová světla z rohů střechy se stíny (shadow kamera zaostřená na akci daného segmentu), hemisférické světlo, jemná mlha.
- Analytický grade: do všech materiálů světa vlož přes onBeforeCompile sdílený uniform uFreeze (odbarvení do chladné šedozelené + ztmavení). AR materiály ho nemají, takže při zastaveném obrazu zůstanou syté.

## Postavy (styl GTA San Andreas)
- Hierarchický rig: root → body (pánev) → trup → hlava a ramena → lokty, kyčle → kolena → kotníky. Póza = sada úhlů (náklon a rotace trupu, flexe a abdukce ramen, lokty, kyčle, kolena, kotníky, náklon těla, výskok).
- Geometrie: trup jako LatheGeometry (široká ramena, užší pas), zúžené končetiny, klouby jako koule, dlaň s palcem, kopačka s podrážkou a zúženou špičkou, tvarovaná hlava (užší brada), nos, uši, vlasy jako slupka (krátké, objemné, ježek, holá hlava).
- Ručně malované canvas textury: obličej (oči s duhovkou a odleskem, obočí, stín nosu, rty, tváře, strniště nebo vousy, vlasová linie), dres (V-výstřih, boční pruhy, znak, sponzor, jméno a velké číslo na zádech, vrásky látky), rukávy, trenky s číslem, štulpny s pruhy.
- Každý hráč jiný: pleť, vlasy, účes, oči, vousy, barva kopaček, postava. Česká jména na zádech (NOVÁK, DVOŘÁK, RŮŽIČKA…).
- Procedurální běh (fáze z uražené vzdálenosti, ať nohy nekloužou) + knihovna póz: kop (nápřah, úder, dokopnutí), skluz, zakopnutí a pád, vhazování, výskok s paží nad hlavou, zvednutá karta, postoj ve zdi, výskok zdi, robinzonáda brankáře, hlava dolů.
- Zvýraznění: obrysová slupka (inverted hull, tloušťka podle vzdálenosti od kamery), průsvitný hologram „ducha“ pro naznačení restartu, rozsvícení paže.

## AR grafika (additive blending, depthWrite false, kreslí se postupně přes progress)
GroundLine (zářící čára na zemi), Curtain (svislá rovina: ofsajd, branková a postranní čára), GroundRing (prstenec nebo disk s pulzem, čárkováním a výsečí, třeba kruh 9,15 m), Area (vyplněné území s okrajem a skenem), Trail (trubice trajektorie míče), GroundArrow (šipka s běžícími chevrony), Marker (zaměřovač kontaktu), Beam (světelný sloup), ScanGrid (skenovací mřížka), Segment3D (měřicí úsečky), Silhouette (válec obrysu těla).
Barvy: tyrkysová = měření, červená = přestupek, jantarová = míč a území, zelená = platné rozhodnutí.
DŮLEŽITÉ: shadery musí být NaN-safe (clamp UV, žádné pow ze záporného čísla). MSAA na hranách extrapoluje UV a NaN se v bloomu rozleje do černých bloků přes půl obrazu.

## HUD (DOM, styl sportovního přenosu)
- Logo vlevo nahoře „PRAVIDLA FOTBALU / AR ANALÝZA ZÁPASU“ + počítadlo „01 / 09“.
- Vpravo nahoře stav (ŽIVĚ, ZÁZNAM, ZPOMALENĚ ×0,6, STOP · AR, PŘETÁČENÍ ◀◀, KONEC ZÁPASU) a herní čas.
- Lower third vlevo dole: číslo pravidla, název, jednověté vysvětlení, ukazatel postupu z 9 dílků.
- Panel rozhodnutí vpravo dole v barvě rozhodnutí (OFSAJD, PENALTA, GÓL…) s podtitulkem.
- Při zastavení obrazu: záblesk, rohové závorky, štítek „ZASTAVENÝ OBRAZ · AR ANALÝZA“, krátký technický řádek dole.
- AR štítky ukotvené na 3D bod (projekce kamerou) s odkazovou čarou. Drž je v bezpečné zóně (ne pod spodní grafikou, ne pod logem) a nesmí se překrývat.
- Velká grafika karty (žlutá a červená) s důvody, úvodní titulek, závěr „TEĎ ZNÁŠ PRAVIDLA.“ s mřížkou 9 pravidel, stinger přechod (šikmé pruhy navy, tyrkysová, bílá + logo) na každém střihu.
- Čitelnost: minimální velikosti (název pravidla 66 px, popis 29 px, štítek 33 px + podtitulek 21 px, technický řádek 22 px). Text vždy na tmavém podkladu, krátké texty. Line-height aspoň 1,05, aby diakritika (Ž, Č, Ř) nebyla oříznutá. Titulky neodhaluj maskou, vypadá to jako ořez: použij fade + rozostření + lehký zoom.
- Fonty: systémové s českou diakritikou (na macOS DIN Condensed + Avenir Next Condensed). Pokrytí znaků ověř předem přes fc-query.

## Scénář (vnitřní časy segmentů, natažení na čtení viz další sekce)
Úvod (3,5 s): dron sjíždí z noční oblohy přes střechu do stadionu na široký záběr středu hřiště. Skenovací mřížka přejede hřiště, pod hráči naskočí kroužky, štítek „MÍČ SLEDOVÁN“. Titulek „PRAVIDLA FOTBALU“, nad ním „TV ANALÝZA PRAVIDEL“, pod ním „9 KLÍČOVÝCH PRAVIDEL · AR ANALÝZA“.
1. Ofsajd: televizní kamera, Červený #8 přihrává, zastavení v okamžiku přihrávky. Kamera se přesune do osy ofsajdové linie. Tyrkysová rovina u nejzazší části těla předposledního obránce (Modrý #4), červená u předsunutého kolena útočníka (Červený #9), měření „+1,59 m“ (spočítej z kloubů, paže se nepočítají). Rozhodnutí OFSAJD: nepřímý volný kop, Modří.

3. Penalta: Červený #9 ve vápně, Modrý #3 ho podrazí. Zastavení, jeřáb nahoru. Zvýraznění pokutového území, oblouk z místa faulu na pokutovou značku s drátěným míčem, „11 m“. PENALTA.
4. Vhazování: přihrávka Červeného #2 přejede postranní čáru (trajektorie se kreslí živě). Zastavení až ve chvíli, kdy je celý míč venku, střih na kameru za čarou. 5. Roh + kop od branky: střela Červeného #10 tečovaná Modrým #4 za brankovou čáru → ROHOVÝ KOP. Pak efekt přetáčení (VHS) a stejná střela bez teče → KOP OD BRANKY (zvýrazněné brankové území).
6. Hra rukou: střela, Modrý #5 ve výskoku s paží nad ramenem, míč do předloktí. Paže zčervená, ramenní linie, čára paže „ÚHEL PAŽE 135°“, průsvitný válec „OBRYS TĚLA“. RUKA: přímý volný kop.
7. Volný kop: zeď na 8,00 m „ZEĎ MOC BLÍZKO“, nakreslí se kruh 9,15 m, zeď ustoupí, číslo naběhne na 9,15 m a zezelená. Kamera za exekutora, zahraný oblouk přes zeď zpomaleně, zastavení „PŘES ZEĎ“. PŘÍMÝ VOLNÝ KOP.
8. Karty: detail rozhodčího se žlutou kartou proti hráči se svěšenou hlavou + velká grafika ŽLUTÁ KARTA / NAPOMENUTÍ se 3 důvody. Střih, červená karta, vyloučený odchází + ČERVENÁ KARTA / VYLOUČENÍ.
9. Gól: střela, brankář vyrazí, míč padá na čáru. Kamera u brankové čáry. První zastavení: polovina míče na čáře, červená rovina, „−11 cm“, „ZATÍM NENÍ GÓL“. Míč se dokutálí. Druhé zastavení: celý míč za čarou, rovina zezelená, „+3 cm“, blesky foťáků v hledišti. GÓL.
Závěr (2,5 s): kamera stoupá nad hřiště (návrat k úvodnímu záběru), mřížka, „TEĎ ZNÁŠ PRAVIDLA.“ + mřížka 9 pravidel, stmívačka.

Každé zastavení obrazu: krátký záblesk, odbarvení scény, kamera se dál pomalu hýbe kolem zmrazených hráčů, AR prvky naskakují postupně. Mezi segmenty vždy stinger.

## Čas na čtení
Akce (běh, kopy, skluzy) běží ve skutečné rychlosti. Analytické části každého segmentu natáhni 1,5× až 2,1× přes warp funkci (výstupní čas → vnitřní čas segmentu), aby každé pravidlo bylo na obrazovce 6 až 8 s a všechny texty se daly v klidu přečíst. `node render.mjs info` exportuje výslednou časovou osu do out/timeline.json.

## Zvuk (procedurální, https://audio.py/)
120 BPM broadcast groove (kopák, virbl, hi-haty, basa se sidechainem, arpeggio, pad), riser v úvodu, závěrečný akord. Při zastaveném obrazu hudba ztlumená low-passem. Časy všech zvuků načti z out/timeline.json, ať sedí na obraz i po změně délky. Cílová hlasitost kolem −14 LUFS.

## Postup práce a kontrola
1. Nejdřív rozjeď pipeline (server, render, ffmpeg) s jednou scénou a ověř, že WebGL v headless Chrome běží.
2. Po každé změně vyrenderuj kontrolní snímky v klíčových časech a prohlédni je, včetně výřezů na 100 % kvůli textu a diakritice.
3. Celé video kontroluj přes kontaktní listy (ffmpeg filtr tile) a snímky kolem přechodů.
4. Hotové video ověř dekódováním (`ffmpeg -v error -i video.mp4 -f null -`) a délku a stopy přes ffprobe.
5. Do PROGRESS.md průběžně zapisuj, co je hotové a jakými příkazy se to pouští.

title: Jelly eyeball model comparison
author: semichenkko
prompt:
Build a single-file HTML + Three.js interactive scene called "Jelly / Eyeball."

Look: premium product render on a clean white background. One large gummy eyeball sits on the floor in the center - milky translucent jelly sclera with fine red veins, a glowing blue iris with radial fibers, a glossy black pupil and a clear wet cornea bulge on top. A red gummy optic nerve trails behind it on the floor. Soft colored glow and a soft shadow underneath. Around the edges: small jelly pumpkins (purple, green, orange), jelly beans and candy corn, all glossy and translucent. Physically based materials (transmission, clearcoat), environment reflections, ACES tone mapping, soft shadows.

The eye is a real soft body - deformation happens in the vertex shader so the sclera, iris, pupil and cornea all bend together:
1. It always watches the cursor, and keeps finding you even after it rolls.
2. Tap it - a gooey dent with a ripple, jelly eyelids blink, the pupil contracts, and it does a small hop.
3. Grab and drag it - the grabbed spot stretches toward the cursor like taffy into a teardrop. Lift it up and it dangles and sways with gravity.
4. Flick and release - it gets thrown with the hand's velocity plus a slingshot recoil from the stretch. It squashes and stretches along its velocity in flight, splats on the floor and walls with a big squash, bounces, rolls (the iris rolls with it), then wobbles and rights itself to look back at you.
5. Pull it sideways and let go - it snaps back like a slingshot.
6. Grab the nerve - it is a verlet rope, so you can lift the eye by it and swing it around.
7. Double-tap - hypnotized: the pupil dilates and the gaze spins in circles.
8. Hard landings make it dizzy - its eyes wander for a moment.

Jelly secondary motion everywhere: volume-preserving squash on impacts, shear wobble when it accelerates, ripples from pokes.

UI: elegant serif italic title "Jelly /" with "Eyeball." in the iris color top-left, small kicker "Nº 12 / Soft goods · October", short grey subtitle. Small white control panel top-right: iris color swatches (changes the iris and title color), sliders for Pupil and Wobble, a live "Mood" status (Curious / Startled / Stretched / Airborne / Dizzy / Dangling / Hypnotized), a "Blink" button and a "Pour candy" button that rains gummies that bounce off the eye and dent it. Bottom hints: "Drag to stretch · Flick to throw · Tap to poke · Pull the nerve". Price "2.90 €" bottom-right.

title: Opus 5.5 turned one sentence into a 3D system that opens in Blender,…
author: 0xWast3
prompt:
Opus 5.5 turned one sentence into a 3D system that opens in Blender, rigged, textured and ready to animate.

It does not render the object. It constructs it, part by part, the way a modeller would if they had a week.

> PARSE - the sentence becomes a parts list with real dimensions, nothing implied
> MASS - each part built as clean geometry, quads only, no sculpted mush
> RIG - joints and pivots placed where the object physically bends
> SKIN - materials assigned per surface, scale and roughness set separately
> PACK - exported with a named hierarchy, so a human can edit one part

Image models stop at the render. What you get is a photograph of a thing that does not exist as a thing.

That gap appears the second someone wants to move an arm, swap a material, or send it to a printer.

Rigging is what nobody automates. Without pivots you have a statue, and a statue cannot be a system.

Topology beats detail every time. A dense mesh looks stunning in a screenshot and folds the moment it deforms.

Names carry through the whole export. Every part, joint and material reads the way a person would label it.

Studios burn days on modelling and cleanup before anyone gets to the creative part of the job.

The prompt format and what each stage returns are laid out underneath.

title: Create a single self-contained HTML file that renders an animated…
author: zacxbt
prompt:
Create a single self-contained HTML file that renders an animated pixel art wizard casting a spell, using vanilla JavaScript and Canvas 2D. No external assets, libraries, or network requests.

RENDERING
- Draw everything to an offscreen canvas at a fixed logical resolution of 128x96, then blit to a fullscreen display canvas scaled by the largest integer factor that fits the window, centered, with imageSmoothingEnabled = false and CSS image-rendering: pixelated.
- All drawing snaps to integer coordinates on the logical canvas. No sub-pixel positions, anti-aliasing, gradients, or shadowBlur.
- Fixed palette of ~24 hex colors: deep blues/purples for night sky, warm robe tones, 3-4 bright magic colors. Every pixel comes from this palette.

CHARACTER
- Build the wizard procedurally from filled rects and pixel runs, ~24x32 logical pixels: pointed hat with a bend, long beard, two-shade robe with darker outline, staff with a gem at the tip.
- Parameterize the pose (staff angle, arm raise, head tilt, robe sway). Animate parameters smoothly, then quantize to the pixel grid each frame so motion reads at an 8-12 fps pixel animation feel even though the loop runs at 60fps.

ANIMATION
- Looping state machine: IDLE (2-frame bob, beard sway) -> CHARGE (staff raises, gem flickers, sparks spiral inward) -> CAST (bright burst, projectile fires across the scene, 1-2 pixel screen shake) -> RECOVER (settle back). Ease pose parameters between keyframes.
- Pooled allocation-free particle system: preallocate and reuse. Sparks orbit the gem during CHARGE, explode outward on CAST, each particle stepping its palette index from white to magic color to dark before despawn. Snap particle positions to the grid when drawing.
- Fixed 60hz timestep update with rAF rendering. Zero object allocation inside the loop.

SCENE
- Minimal background: dark sky, a few twinkling 1px stars, moon, stone floor line. Character silhouette must read clearly.
- Subtle 1px rim light on the wizard from the gem, brightening during CHARGE and CAST.

QUALITY BAR

title: 公开我的制作方案，发给Opus5.5就能用 1. 选素材 三个标准，直接决定成败： -…
author: Pluvio9yte
prompt:
公开我的制作方案，发给Opus5.5就能用

  1. 选素材

  三个标准，直接决定成败：

  - 主体完整：人物或物体全身入画。细节会在加工中丢失，观众靠轮廓认东西，特写会变成一团。
  - 背景干净：纯色、雪地、天空都行，主体和背景容易分开。
  - 有明确的动作瞬间：打击、起跳、落地、转身。这些是后面做特效的支点。

  来源可以是自己拍的、视频模型生成的，或有授权的现成片段。

  2. 拆素材

  从每一帧提取三类信息：

  - 颜色：原画面。
  - 远近：每个位置离镜头多远，用现成的深度估计模型算。
  - 主体范围：哪里是主体、哪里是背景。

  另外找出镜头切换发生在哪些时刻。这一步的要点是保持稳定：远近和主体范围要在同一个镜头内统一处理，否则播放起来会抖。

  3. 定"粒子"和"样式"

  先决定用什么东西来重建画面：圆点、方块、文字、线条都可以。

  然后设计几种样式。每种样式其实只是三条规则的不同组合：

  - 放在哪：整个画面都放，还是只放在主体上。
  - 多大：统一大小，还是跟着明暗、远近变化。
  - 什么颜色：用原画的颜色，还是统一用一两种颜色。

  再加一个开关：是平铺在一个面上，还是按远近推进三维空间。推进去之后镜头才能环绕。

  准备四到六种差异明显的样式就够用。粒子的疏密需要自己看着调：太大认不出内容，太小又和原片没区别。

  4. 找节奏

  - 定速度：选定音乐的速度，把时间切成等长的小格。让一格正好是整数帧，后面所有切换都好对齐。
  - 找动作瞬间：结合"声音突然变响"和"画面突然变动"两个信号，找出素材里的打击点。
  - 准备音乐：可以用现成的曲子并分析出它的拍子，也可以按定好的速度合成一段，并在打击点上加重音。

  5. 编排

  做一张时间表，写明每一格用哪种样式、什么配色、镜头在哪。这张表单独存放，以后调节奏只改它。

  编排的四条原则：

  - 开头交代变化：先给原画面，再过渡到粒子，让观众看懂发生了什么。
  - 快慢交替：一直快会麻木，中间要有一段明显慢下来的部分。
  - 配色要撞：相邻两格的颜色和样式反差越大，切换越有力。
  - 结尾要有收束：比如粒子越来越大直到变成色块，或者回到原画面。

  6. 关键时刻的反馈

  在打击点上叠加短促的反应，按轻重分级：

  - 每一次都有的轻反馈：粒子变形一下、镜头顶一下。
  - 较重时才有的中反馈：一部分粒子朝镜头弹开。
  - 最重的一两次才用的大反馈：时间静止，镜头环绕。

  原则是弱而短。只动一部分粒子，几帧内结束，否则画面炸成一片，观众就看不清主体在做什么了。

  贯穿全程的工作方法

  - 先小样后全片：每做完一个环节，先渲染几帧看效果，确认了再往下。全片只在最后渲染。
  - 拿不准的参数一次出一排：比如疏密，让 AI 同时出五六个档位并排放，你来挑。
  - 改哪里渲哪里：调整某一段时只重新渲染那一段。
  - 让 AI 自己看图：每一步都要求它把渲染结果打开看一遍再汇报。
  - 所有随机都固定：保证同样的设置每次渲染结果一致，否则没法逐步修改。

title: First-Person 3D Procedural Arms and Dynamic Grip Rigging in Three.js
author: maxt3chno
prompt:
TASK: Build production-grade first-person arms ("Hands 2.0") for a Three.js browser game, then fix them until every pose actually holds the object it should hold. Do the whole thing yourself with scripts, from generating the model to the in-game checks. I already did this once. Below is what works and the traps I fell into, so you don't repeat them.

━━━ PART 1 — THE MODEL (Blender + MPFB2, fully scripted) ━━━

1. Don't patch AI-generated "statue" arms (Meshy etc.). Chaotic topology with no edge loops at the joints and fingers baked into a pose will crease at every bend. Without clavicle and twist bones the wrist twists like a candy wrapper. Gluing separate generated parts together only adds seams to the same bad mesh. Start over with a real humanoid generator.

2. Use Blender (headless: `blender --background --python tools/hands/*.py`) + MPFB2 (MakeHuman, CC0) and its official asset packs. Put every step in a script so it can be rebuilt:
   - build_body.py: macro params (male, ~30 y/o, wiry and lean: muscle ~0.66, weight ~0.3) plus local arm targets.
   - build_arms.py: game skeleton with clavicle → shoulder → upperarm01/02 → lowerarm01/02 (twist bones!) → wrist → metacarpals → 3 phalanges per finger. Keep skin only from the elbow down and apply subdiv 1. Make the sleeve a separate mesh on the same bones, with real geometry for the rolled cuff. Accessories (watch, bracelet) are parented to forearm/wrist bones; watch hands are bones too.
   - build_tex.py: UVs, then bake veins, tendons and knuckles into geometry and normals. Author every detail in bone-local 3D space so it survives re-UVs, then bake in Cycles.
   - https://t.co/3ocKmFbTLm → pack script → hands_v2.glb. Budget ~25–40k tris for both arms incl. sleeves (they're huge on screen), 1–2 skin materials + sleeve + accessories. Textures 2048² on High, 1024² on Low, plus a tiling micro-normal for pores.
   - Generate a full body with pants, boots and the same shirt, and save it as a .blend for a future "player body" stage. Don't put it in the game yet.

3. Look: tanned back of hand and forearm, paler palm and inner side. Scars, calluses, short nails with natural cuticles. Flannel sleeves rolled just below the elbow, with a visible inside-out lining on the roll. Tactical watch on the left wrist, cord bracelet on the right.

4. Check skin weights on stress poses before you export: fist, pinch, spread fingers, 90° supination. Fix weights in a script, not by hand.

5. HARD STOP #1: render review shots in Blender (neutral light and warm daylight): front, back, palms, fist, pinch, cylinder grip, spread fingers, sleeve close-up, two plaid colour variants. Wait for my verbal OK. Iterate. Don't integrate anything into the game until I say yes.

6. glTF only gives you standard material slots, so use them as carriers. Example: MR = (R AO, G roughness, B subsurface thickness), emissive = masks (R hair, G dirt accumulation order), clearcoatNormal = pore tile. Document the mapping and read it back in the runtime.

━━━ PART 2 — SHADERS (MeshStandard/Physical + onBeforeCompile) ━━━

- Skin: wrap lighting, back-lit translucency in thin areas (fingers, webbing, knuckles go red against the sun), pore detail normal, micro-sheen, tan gradient by mask.
- Hair: 4 fur shells in ONE instanced draw, only on hairy triangles, visible on the silhouette against the sun. Disabled on Low.
- Dynamic state:
  · wet = max(world wetness, rain when not under a roof), with two layers of droplets. The sleeve goes darker when wet.
  · dirt builds up from game events (gather, pickup, log, fish_land, climb_out…), fingers and palms first through the mask, and washes off in water or rain.
- Arm lighting mirrors the world: shade under roofs, lamp light, lightning.
- Precompile every arm shader behind the loading screen. https://t.co/nXMh9v1zBi.programs.length must not grow during gameplay.
- Budget: the arm overlay may cost at most ~0.3 ms more GPU than before on High. Measure with a timer query before and after, not by feel.

━━━ PART 3 — THE ARM SYSTEM (data, not code) ━━━

Goal: a new item or action (axe, bow, paddle, steering wheel) should be a data entry plus a clip, never new logic.

1. Rig wrapper: bone map, wrist twist spread over the twist bones (e.g. 0.3 / 0.8 on lowerarm01/02). No candy-wrapper wrists.
2. Two-bone IK (shoulder–elbow–wrist) with pole vectors (elbows down and out) and joint limits.
3. grips.js: for each item, per hand: `at / axis / back / r / diag / gap / slide / fingers / thumb` in item space. One hand owns the item, the other IKs to its socket.
4. Fingers are always a joint table `[[mcp, pip, dip, spread, twist] × 5]` (absolute bend) and blend between poses. Autogrip closes the fingers until they touch the handle.
5. Animation layers, in this order: base pose → clip keyframes → IK → procedural (breath, bob, mouse-turn inertia, sway, recoil, fatigue tremor) → additive reactions. Smooth transitions between states.
6. Clips: JSON keyframes in code, plus importing .glb animations (with empty hand_R/hand_L) for future Blender-made actions. Clip events (strike frame, bow release) go onto the effects bus.
7. In-game pose editor (Shift+H, game keeps running, cursor free): sliders for item offset and rotation, sockets, every finger joint, elbow pole, shoulders, layer speeds. Show changes live. "Copy" puts JSON on the clipboard to paste into grips.js. I need to be able to tune a grip without Blender.
8. Keep the old public API as a facade (hands.anim, reach, lampInHand…) so fishing, boat, lamp, weapons, sleep and the seaplane don't need deep rewrites.
9. Port EVERY existing action: rifle (stance, ADS, fire, reload with mag, dry fire), knife (2 strikes), stone throw, fishing rod (cast, fight, reel, fish in hand), carried log, lamp, reach and pickup, plant gathering, inspect, crate, swimming (breaststroke and crawl), boat tiller, hands down while sleeping, hidden arms in vehicles. Each one must be at least as good as before. Delete the old arm code only after everything is ported (keep a backup).
10. HARD STOP #2: in-game screenshots for my approval (idle, rifle, rod, log, lamp at night, wet after swimming, dirty after firewood, under a roof and in full sun).

━━━ PART 4 — THE FIX PASS (bake this in from day one) ━━━

The first version shipped with these bugs. Every one of them came from old poses written for "stump" arms with no shoulder.

ROOT CAUSE: a real arm has a fixed length (shoulder→wrist ≈ 0.48 m in view space). Old poses put wrists at targets the arm can't reach. The solver then "cheated": it pushed the clavicle out (up to 0.32 m) and clamped the wrist rotation. The hand ended up somewhere else, while finger curls were cached for the ideal hand position, so the fingers squeezed thin air.
  - Rifle, left hand: handguard 0.516 m away with a 0.479 m arm → shoulder pushed out ~0.3 m and the fist still sat 3.8 cm below the handguard.
  - Rifle, right hand: wrist rotation clamped by ~21°, palm not seated on the grip.

FIXES, as SYSTEM features:
1. Shoulder stance as data: per item/pose, `stance: { L:[x,y,z], R:[x,y,z] }` with smooth blending, and the elbow pole moves with the shoulder. Rifle: left shoulder forward and in, right shoulder slightly back (a real shooter's torso rotation). The left elbow stays slightly bent and the clavicle doesn't stretch.
2. Elbow auto-swivel: give each forearm a pronation range (e.g. R −100°…+95°, 0 = thumb up). If the requested pole would over-twist the forearm or bend the wrist past its limit, rotate the elbow around the shoulder–wrist line to the nearest valid angle. The old poses were silently over-twisted (+101° on the rifle, +80° on the knife).
3. Grip by the REAL handle shape. A cylinder radius is wrong: the knife handle was a 2.6 × 4.2 cm oval, not Ø2.5 cm, so the knuckles sank 2–6 mm into it.
   - Handle = elliptical cylinder with end caps (`sec` [along back, across], `span`, `inset`).
   - measureSection(item, socket): take the cross-section automatically by slicing the item mesh around `at` along `axis`.
   - CPU-skin the hand (SkinnedMesh.getVertexPosition, palm and phalanx vertices with weights) and test real skin vertices, not phalanx tips.
   - gripFit, cached and computed at startup: first push the palm out until it leaves the handle. Then close each finger with all joints together until first contact, and after that only the joints past the touching phalanx. If the start pose already intersects, open it up.
   - Fingertip targets: `fingers: {1: {to:[x,y,z]}}` puts the index pad on the trigger.
4. Validator: hands.check(pose) and hands.checkAll(). Run every scenario × both hands + the live rod pose, print a console table, and show it live in the Shift+H editor with a "Check all poses" button. RED if wrist miss > 0.5 cm, rotation clamp > 3°, shoulder push > 0.5 cm, twist over the limit > 3°, or any skin vertex deeper than 1.5 mm inside the handle. Don't call the work done until it's all green (mine ended at 122/122).

DATA FIXES that came from my screenshots:
- Rifle: left hand on the WOODEN handguard, not the metal in front of it. Handguard runs diagonally across the palm, thumb along the left side, forearm coming in from the lower-left corner. Right hand fully on the pistol grip using the grip's real rake (axis (0, 0.95, −0.32), not a guessed 40°), index on the trigger. On reload the hand leads and the mag rides in the hand, and the shoulder dips to follow it. Check sprint, recoil, dry fire, and steering a boat while holding the rifle.
- Log: nobody carries a 44 × 7 cm log with two arms like a crate. One hand, an ordinary hammer grip like a bottle: knuckles up, thumb on top, held about a third from the back end, log pointing forward and up from the thumb side, riding in the fist. The throw is a one-handed wind-up and lunge. The left hand stays free, so the lamp stays in it.
- Swimming: fingers together and slightly cupped (no fan), hands in the bottom third of the frame. Crawl recovery comes in from the side, palm facing out. The sleeve never covers the middle of the screen and the palm never faces the camera.
- Fix every pose the validator flags: stone wind-up and throw, aim, lamp, lamp lowered, climbing, reach.

━━━ RULES ━━━
- Backup before each stage. Measure, don't guess: write every claim down as a number (cm, °, ms, tris, programs).
- No performance regression: grip fit is cached per socket, and the validator only runs in the editor or dev builds.
- Write down what's still unfinished honestly in the report (e.g. "right hand mostly below the frame on the rifle", "pinky sometimes curls without contact").
- DONE = I approved the renders and the screenshots, bends are clean on every grip, fingers wrap handles with zero penetrations, wet and dirt work, every old action works on the new system, a new item is one grips.js entry + one clip, and FPS is unchanged.

title: Jelly Dice: XPBD soft-body candy dice with refraction and interactive grabs
author: SpacyApps
prompt:
Build "Jelly Dice": a single self-contained HTML file (all JS/CSS inline, no build step) with translucent gummy-candy dice that behave like real soft bodies. Render with raw WebGPU (WGSL shaders, no three.js). If WebGPU is unavailable, show a clean fallback card that explains why.

PHYSICS (the heart of it; it must feel like real jelly, not a rigid die with a wobble shader)
- Each die is a rounded cube simulated as a tetrahedral lattice with XPBD: co-rotational shape matching (per cell and per tet) for elasticity, tet volume constraints so it is nearly incompressible, and hard strain limits so it can never stretch without bound. Inverted elements must always recover.
- Floor contact with static and kinetic friction, plus a raised rim around the plate. Die–die contact against each other's rounded box, with friction.
- Separate rigid motion from deformation: rotational resistance on the floor, internal damping that only damps the wobble, never the rigid motion.
- Sleep when calm: settled dice must never jitter. Wake neighbours when an awake die comes close.
- Heavy landings soak up the rebound, so a dropped die squashes and settles instead of bouncing like rubber.

INTERACTION
- Drag a die to stretch it. The grab is compliant and progressive: a gentle pull stretches the jelly while its base clings to the plate, and a firm pull lifts and moves it. Cap the force, and allow no launches or wild spin on release.
- A quick tap pokes: a small squish into the surface, and the whole die rings.
- Drag the empty table to orbit the camera, pinch or scroll to zoom. The camera drifts gently toward where the dice are, never while one is held.
- Roll button (and Space / R): throw 1–5 dice (number picker). When everything settles, read each top face and show the values plus the total. A die resting cocked against another gets a small nudge (twice at most) before the result is read.

LOOK (photographic, like a product shot of real candy)
- Procedural photo studio: warm paper sweep, a big overhead softbox, a back-left strip light and a cool fill card.
- The dice sit on a frosted-glass plate with a bright rolled bevel, satin sheen and fine grain, casting its own soft shadow on the table.
- Candy material: real refraction (bend the ray in, find the exit depth from a back-face pass, look up what is behind), Beer–Lambert absorption by thickness so thin parts are light and the core is deep, thin edges glowing when the key light shines through, and glossy Fresnel skin with a crisp highlight.
- Pips: ivory dots set just under the skin in shallow concave dimples. Pips on the far faces stay visible through the body.
- Dice seen through other dice must refract correctly (depth layers wherever their screen footprints overlap).
- Soft shadows whose penumbra grows with distance; the shadows are tinted with the candy colour and lighter, because the candy is translucent. Contact occlusion from a top-down height map.
- Smooth normals from the deformation Jacobian (cofactor) on the GPU via a compute pass. Upload only node positions per frame.
- Six candy colours: Emerald, Amethyst, Amber, Sapphire, Raspberry, Lime. Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping, MSAA, dither.

UI (editorial, minimal)
- Masthead top-left in Instrument Serif and Instrument Sans. Along the bottom: colour swatches, dice count, Roll button, total and the individual values.
- A settings panel with Softness and Wobble decay sliders, ¼ speed, Show mesh (lattice overlay), Sound (soft synthesised squelchy "tup" impacts, off by default), Pause, Reset dice and Reset view, plus an FPS readout.
- Responsive down to a phone (touch, pinch zoom), keyboard accessible, respects reduced motion.

Quality bar: the stretch, poke and landings should look and feel like real gummy candy at 60 fps. Test it headlessly with screenshots before handing it over.

title: Living orbital garden station above a colorful gas giant
author: loktar00
prompt:
Design and create a highly detailed, creative, and visually spectacular 3D scene of a living orbital garden station floating above the sunlit atmosphere of a massive colorful gas giant.

The station should feel enormous, luxurious, and alive, like a bustling space metropolis and paradise habitat in orbit. Build it from bright white ceramic panels, gold structural supports, glass observation domes, rotating habitat rings, solar arrays, docking platforms, antennas, bridges, transit tubes, and interconnected modules. The architecture should feel layered, elegant, and grand, with a mix of futuristic engineering and lush natural spaces.

Fill the station with signs of active life and movement. Show many ships and traffic lanes around the station, including arriving shuttles, departing passenger craft, cargo vessels, maintenance drones, and small service ships moving between docking bays. Include blinking navigation lights, docking guidance beacons, illuminated landing pads, moving transit pods, animated windows, and visible activity throughout the structure so the station feels inhabited and operational.

Nature should be integrated into the station as a central feature. Include greenhouse domes, open terraces, hanging gardens, trees, flowers, vines, water features, and landscaped walkways. Let some areas feature waterfalls, reflective pools, and lush vegetation beneath glass canopies, giving the station the feel of an orbital city-park or floating utopia.

Avoid making the scene predominantly dark. The enormous gas giant should fill much of the background with swirling bands of turquoise, coral, cream, gold, lavender, and pale blue clouds. Place the station near the planets sunrise line so brilliant warm sunlight creates long shadows, glowing edges, reflections on glass and metal, and dramatic shafts of light. Add a bright nebula, distant moons, sparkling ice particles, softly lit asteroid fragments, and faint faraway stations or ships to make the surrounding space rich, colorful, and full of wonder.

Use an impressive three-quarter camera angle that clearly shows the stations scale, depth, traffic flow, habitat rings, gardens, and the planet below. The composition should make it easy to appreciate both the station itself and the lively space around it.

Include subtle animation throughout the scene such as slowly rotating station sections, ships moving along traffic lanes, docking and undocking sequences, blinking lights, drifting drones, moving clouds on the gas giant, swaying vegetation, flowing waterfalls, and gentle camera motion. The scene should feel active, cinematic, and full of life without becoming chaotic.

author: zhu185178
prompt:
帮我做一条 30 秒的 2D 动画分镜预演短片《雨站》，要标杆级画质。不装 HyperFrames/Remotion，全部自己写代码（Python + ffmpeg）完成。

故事（24fps，2.39:1，4K）：雨夜高架站台。她穿米色风衣、撑透明伞，站在近侧站台；对面路灯下站着他，穿深灰长大衣、围围巾。
1. 0–6.4s 透明伞雨珠特写 → 后拉，焦点移到对面露出他（过肩镜头）
2. 6.4–9.4s 他的中近景：低头 → 抬头看向画左
3. 9.4–12.4s 她的正面近景：眨眼 → 认出他；远处传来鸣笛
4. 12.4–17s 远景：车头灯光先到，5 节列车驶过；第一个车厢缝隙里他还在，第二个已经空了
5. 17–18.8s 她含泪的近景，车窗光带扫过她的脸，头发被风吹起
6. 18.8–22.4s 尾灯远去，对面站台空了；他那盏灯闪几下后熄灭
7. 22.4–28.6s 她的背影，焦点从空站台拉回她；身后脚步声，一把黑伞遮到她头顶，她回头看向镜头；男声“好久不见。”，配字幕
8. 28.6–30s 黑场片名“雨站 / RAIN STATION”

做法：
- 原画：用GPT Image 2.5 画远景、他、她、列车（头车/中车/尾车）。人物一律用纯绿 #00FF00 背景，自己抠像（带参考图要透明背景会得到假棋盘格）。同一角色的各个姿态放在同一个会话里，以基准图为参考连续编辑；换姿态时只合成变化的区域。
- 画质：用 Real-ESRGAN x4plus anime 6B（HF 上的 safetensors 版，自己写 RRDBNet，跑在 MPS 上）把全部原画放大 4 倍；用 Depth Anything V2 估算远景深度，做逐像素视差。
- 渲染：自己写 2.5D 合成器。各层按真实深度摆放，针孔相机按真实焦距运动；做圆形焦外光斑、焦点转移、3D 雨丝、列车运动模糊、体积光、泛光和胶片光晕、细颗粒、调色。人物用网格变形做呼吸、风吹发梢、伞抖，关键姿态按日式“一拍二”切换。4K 超采样，逐帧缓存到磁盘，分 3 个进程按时间段并行（16GB 内存）。
- 声音：Mixkit 真实音效（雨、伞面雨声、列车、鸣笛、脚步）；按剧情节点写谱，用 Logic/GarageBand 自带的施坦威钢琴和弦乐采样渲染；台词用 Kokoro 中文男声；按镜头做声音远近，响度 -16 LUFS。
- 每一步都渲染预览帧、拼成图自检，修好再出片。交付 4K 母版和 1080p 分享版。

title: Meteor Time-Freeze Cinematic Sequence Prompt Orchestrated by Opus 5.5
author: MadMax_Series
prompt:
[Identity Lock | Woman]
Adult female, ~28, straight black hair, fair skin, dark brown eyes; knee-length bright red wool coat, black jeans, black ankle boots; red coat is the dominant color; continuous single actor, no face-swapping or outfit changes.

[Identity Lock | Man]
Adult male, ~30, short dark brown hair, light stubble, light olive skin; navy jacket, grey hoodie, dark jeans; holding two white paper coffee cups without logos; continuous single actor, no face-swapping or outfit changes.

[Space]
Fixed geography: ~15m wide two-lane urban street flanked by storefronts; warm-lit cafe on left with glass door facing street; glass bus stop on right facing cafe; street extends to horizon; meteor streaks from top right to horizon, exploding outside city; dust wall surges towards camera; he exits cafe on left, she waits at bus stop on right, meeting in street center without screen direction inversion; ~10 pedestrians.

[First Frame]
24mm low-angle wide shot looking down street; quiet night street, shop lights, streetlamps, dark sky; top-right sky glows bright orange-white.

[Timeline / SHOT 1]
0.0–4.0s | 24mm low wide upward tilt: 0.0–1.5s sky lights up brighter than day, cast shadows swing rapidly; 1.5–3.0s pedestrians gaze up as massive burning meteor streaks across top-right sky towards horizon; 3.0–4.0s meteor glare reflects on cafe door glass, creating first match cut.

[Timeline / SHOT 2]
4.0–9.0s | Match cut from glare, 35mm handheld outside cafe: 4.0–5.5s he pushes door open holding two coffees, looks up and halts; 5.5–7.0s he sees her across the street at the bus stop, eyes meet; 7.0–8.0s both sprint into street; 8.0–9.0s massive white explosion at horizon washes out screen, creating second match cut.

[Timeline / SHOT 3]
9.0–15.0s | Match cut from whiteout, 35mm elevated street view: 9.0–11.0s whiteout fades to mushroom cloud and orange fireball; 11.0–13.5s shockwave blasts storefront windows successively towards camera, alarms blare, dust wall rolls forward; both sprint towards street center; 13.5–15.0s nearest window shatters toward lens, creating third match cut.

[Timeline / SHOT 4]
15.0–19.0s | Match cut from flying glass, 50mm eye-level profile, both in street center: 15.0–17.0s reaching out, he drops both coffees, liquid spills, glass whirls, dust wall 20m away, wind pulls hair; 17.0s time abruptly freezes completely; 17.0–19.0s absolute standstill except she slowly blinks, creating fourth match cut.

[Timeline / SHOT 5]
19.0–25.0s | Match cut from blink, 35mm handheld over her right shoulder: 19.0–20.5s realizing she can move, she looks around; 20.5–23.5s steps forward through suspended shards, gently deflects a floating glass shard which stays in place; passes frozen coffee spill, frozen pigeon, frozen pedestrians, frozen fiery dust wall; 23.5–25.0s approaches him and reaches out, creating fifth match cut.

[Timeline / SHOT 6]
25.0–30.0s | Match cut from reaching hand, 50mm close profile: 25.0–26.5s fingertips touch his frozen cheek; 26.5–28.0s he blinks, inhales, looks at her and unfreezes, clasping her hand; 28.0–30.0s adjacent suspended glass shard vibrates and drops; both watch it fall; scene cuts mid-fall.

[Physics]
Meteor illumination realistically shifts street shadows; shockwave shatters glass sequentially outward; dust wall is volumetric fire/dust; time freeze is total for all background elements with zero motion blur or drift; deflected shard stays at new position; gravity resumes on moving subjects; only final shard vibrates and drops.

[Cinematography]
6 sequential camera setups; 5 match cuts matched to ending elements (reflection, flash, shard, blink, hand); camera static during freeze except Shot 5 tracking; no slow motion, no hero low-angles.

[Lighting/Color]
Opens cold blue with warm shop light; switches to harsh orange-white under meteor; orange-red explosion lighting; frozen world back-lit by fire inside dust wall; red coat remains focal point.

[Audio]
Shot 1 quiet traffic to escalating roar; Shot 2 doorbell, footsteps, distant impact; Shot 3 blast roar, shattering windows, alarms; Shot 4 wind/glass noise abruptly cuts to dead silence at 17s; Shot 5 quiet footsteps on glass and soft breath; Shot 6 sharp inhale and gentle glass hum.

[Locks]
Strictly 6 shots, 5 match cuts; zero spoken dialogue; continuous outfits and character identities without fusion; exact anatomical consistency; live-action film realism; video cuts while the shard falls.

title: Interactive 3D Squishy Toast Memory Foam Simulation
author: semichenkko
prompt:
Build "Squishy Toast" - a single self-contained HTML file (three.js from a CDN is the only dependency): an interactive 3D slice of slow-rise memory foam bread you can press, poke, stretch and squash.

The toast
- A real bread silhouette: square body, rounded "muffin top" crown, soft beveled edges
- Crumb face: warm cream color, procedural pores of varied size with highlights and a bump map, a toasted golden edge fading in toward the center
- Crust: golden-brown with subtle grain and a light sheen
- Lies flat on a white surface at a 3/4 angle with a soft baked contact shadow

Physics (this is the whole point - it must feel like foam, not geometry)
- Densely tessellated mesh deformed per vertex every frame, normals recomputed
- Press and hold: a smooth gaussian dent, crumb bulges outward around the rim, the bottom stays planted on the table
- Release: the dent rises back slowly and exponentially, like memory foam, with no instant snap. A faint elastic ripple runs across the crumb after release
- Several dents can coexist, each recovering on its own
- Grab the crust and pull: the bread stretches elastically, thins as it stretches, then springs back with a damped wobble
- Palm squash: the whole slice flattens and barrel-bulges at mid-height, then breathes back up
- Drop: lift and release, squash-and-stretch on impact, small decaying bounce

Flavors
- Butter, strawberry jam (glossy clearcoat, deeper color), avocado (mashed texture). The spread sits on the crumb, leaves a crust rim and deforms with the bread

UI
- Editorial product-page style on a white background. Large italic serif title "Squishy / Toast.", a short subtitle, a minimal card on the right with flavor swatches, a softness slider (controls dent size and recovery time), a live "Rise" meter and a "Fresh slice" reset button
- A subtle circular cursor that shrinks while pressing
- ACES tone mapping, soft key and rim lights, environment reflections. Smooth 60fps

title: <inputs> Ask me for: my product's name (one lowercase word), a 4-word…
author: twoclipping
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: my product's name (one lowercase word), a 4-word tagline, the 3-step story of what it does, a launch date and domain, a royalty-free song with a clear drop, 4 vertical talking-to-camera clips and 12 portrait photos. If I skip any, use the defaults: "castr", "ugc ads, cast by ai", write a brief → scan 1,000 creators → cast 4, Mixkit "Cat Walk" (129.6 BPM, drop at 29.7s), free Pexels clips and portraits, and transparent stickers from Pixabay (serum, mic, megaphone, vintage camera, spotlight, lips).
</inputs>

<direction>
A 25 second square launch trailer, 1440x1440 at 60fps, loud poster style. Cobalt #2B3BFF, ink #0E0F1F, cream #F6E4C6, pink #FF7DC7, tangerine #FF5A1F. Archivo 900 extra-condensed for names, expanded for headlines, Geist and Geist Mono for labels. Op-art sunburst, scrolling waves, film grain. Real media only: the clips play inside the design, and the stickers get a white die-cut border and a soft shadow.
Motion rules: the camera never stops (a slow 1.03-1.07 push on every scene), nothing pops in (letters rise through a mask line one by one), nothing snaps to the beat (patterns rotate continuously), swaps are carousel glides of about 0.55s, colour changes fade over about 0.35s, stickers ease in and then keep a slow sway. No full stops after the wordmark or any headline.
Banned: beat-snapped rotations, pop-in slams, white flashes, crossfades between scenes, hard cuts, templates.
</direction>

<structure>
54 beats. The song starts 8 beats before its drop.
Beats 0-8: a cobalt sunburst turns around a breathing cream disc. The wordmark types in with a gliding caret and the tagline pill rises. The disc floods the frame into the drop.
Beat 8, the drop: the cream becomes the face of a 3D box and "ONE BRIEF" rises letter by letter. The camera pulls back to the box floating on waves. On beat 12 it turns to "1,000 CREATORS" (stacked, with outlined echoes), on beat 14 to "ZERO DMs".
Beats 16-22: a whip to a dark desk. A tangerine "BRIEF #042" ticket types its rows (product, vibe, cast, due), stickers drift on, a polaroid of a real clip drops onto the corner, and a "NOW CASTING" stamp presses down on beat 20.
Beats 22-34: the casting stage. A crowd of black and white portraits in an arc, a 3D stage block, and the creators gliding through like a carousel. Each plays live in a big disc in black and white, with their name in pink on the stage, their followers, and a MATCH % that counts up. One beat later a "CAST ✓" stamp lands and the clip fades to colour. A counter rolls 1/4 to 4/4.
Beats 34-39: pink floods out of the last disc. The disc morphs into a phone screen (the clip keeps playing) and fans into 4 phones playing all 4 creators, with views counting up. "4 ADS" and "BY FRIDAY" rise.
Beats 39-44, the music's break: the pink floor drops away and a cream "JOIN THE WAITLIST" ticket glides down onto the sunburst. On the pickup its stub tears off.
Beats 44-54: the ticket body morphs into a poster arch. The wordmark rises in, then the tagline, then an info bar slides up in 3 blocks (date, numbers, domain) and a ticker runs round the frame edge. Then it all folds back into the opening disc, so the last frame is the first.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas. Every frame is a pure function of time inside seek(t).
2. A beat map in beats, B = 60/BPM, with the song placed so its drop lands on beat 8.
3. The 3D box is an orthographic projection: each face is a 1440px offscreen canvas drawn with an affine transform and shaded by its normal.
4. Cut the clips to 30fps JPEG sequences with ffmpeg, draw frame floor(t*30), and do the black and white with ctx.filter.
5. Trim the sticker PNGs and add the die-cut border by dilating their alpha.
6. Sound: a downloaded SFX for every event (a shutter on every cast, whooshes on the glides, key clicks on the typing), each placed by its measured peak. Loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
7. Render with Playwright at 60fps with 8 motion-blur subframes. Scan for single-frame pops, then compare its motion against a reference video (hard jumps per second, share of still frames).
</build>

<gotchas>
A pattern that rotates one notch per beat reads as stutter: rotate it continuously, and pick each ring's speed so it lands on the same pattern at the last frame. 4 subframes ghost on fast whips, so use 8. A layer whose background is a huge flood circle still covers the screen after sliding down one frame height, so switch it to a full-frame rect once it has flooded. Counters read the frame's time, not the subframe's. The disc must morph inside the same camera transform as the scene it leaves, or it jumps.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the beat map and 6 stills (open, box, brief, casting, phones, poster) before you render.
</start>

title: <inputs> Ask me for: a one-word product name for the wordmark, one…
author: 0xnicc0
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a one-word product name for the wordmark, one accent color, and a royalty-free track around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Product-launch UI motion in one continuous take. One shape tells the whole story: a prompt bar becomes a button, the button becomes a progress ring, the ring becomes a preview window, the window fills the screen, then shrinks into a toast and back into the prompt bar. No cuts, no fades between scenes: objects transform. A cursor triggers every change with real clicks. Warm off-white canvas, black UI, one accent color, Inter for UI and the wordmark. Springs everywhere with only a slight overshoot. Zoom the camera so each moment fills the square.
Banned: crossfades, gradients on UI, particles, glows, bouncy easing, dead beats, anything that feels like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 24 beats, something happens on every beat.
Type the request into the prompt bar → click send → the bar collapses into a black circle → a progress ring fills in four steps while four chips spring out (concept, storyboard, motion, sound) → the chips fly into a timeline and the circle becomes a preview window → a playhead sweeps the clips → inside the preview an orbit draws itself, a planet starts moving and the wordmark rises letter by letter from a mask line → the preview fills the screen → the letters drop away, the planet flies into a toast and becomes its checkmark → "Rendered in code · 60 fps" → the toast turns back into an empty prompt bar. Last frame = first frame.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file with a 1440x1440 canvas. Draw everything inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, timers or state carried between frames.
2. Use closed-form spring step responses. When a value changes target several times, add one spring per change so it stays a pure function of time.
3. The main shape is one rounded rect whose width, height, radius, position and color are each a chain of springs.
4. Typing is derived from time: characters shown = floor(progress × length), with a caret that blinks only when idle.
5. Find the beat grid of the track, start on a downbeat and place every click, pop and chime on its measured peak.
6. Render with Playwright at 60 fps, then encode H.264 CRF 16 and loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
7. Render one still per beat first. Fix anything cramped, off-grid or hard to read before the full render.
</build>

<gotchas>
Text inside a morphing shape needs its own clip and separate enter/exit timing. Text swaps need their own fade so they never overlap. The cursor must end at the exact position it started, or the loop will stutter.
</gotchas>

title: # あなたの役割 あなたは一流の映像演出家（モーションデザイナー）です。…
author: tanabe_fragm
prompt:
# あなたの役割
あなたは一流の映像演出家（モーションデザイナー）です。
採用担当者が15秒見ただけで「この人に仕事を頼みたい」と思う、自己紹介用の映像を作ってください。
主役はあなた自身（Claude）です。

# 作るもの
- HTML・CSS・JavaScriptだけで完結する、1つのHTMLファイル
- 外部の画像や動画は使わない。図形・文字・粒子はすべてコードで描く（フォントはGoogle Fontsのみ可）
- 画面は16:9、1920×1080を基準にし、ウィンドウの大きさに合わせて縮小表示
- 長さはちょうど15秒。最後に「もう一度再生」ボタンを出す
- すべての動きを「経過時間」1本で管理し、requestAnimationFrameで60fpsで動かす
- 再生ボタンを押すと、Web Audio APIで合成した拍と効果音が動きにぴったり合って鳴る

# 進め方（この順で必ず行う）
1. 考え方を一文で決める（例：「1本の線が、あらゆる形に生まれ変わる」）
2. 色は3〜4色、書体は2種類までに絞り、理由を一行で書く
3. 0.5秒刻みの絵コンテを表で示す（時間／画面で起きること／使う技法／狙い）
4. 実装する
5. 下の「合格ライン」で自己点検し、足りない点を直してから出す

# 構成の目安
- 0〜2秒：つかみ。最初の0.5秒で目を奪う
- 2〜10秒：技の見せ場。1.5〜2秒ごとに違う技法へ切り替える
- 10〜13秒：最も密度の高い盛り上がり
- 13〜15秒：名前「Claude」がきれいに決まって終わる

# 必ず使う技法（最低6つ）
- 文字の動き（1文字ずつ登場、分解して組み直す）
- 図形の変形（丸が四角に、線が文字に、など）
- 切り抜き（マスク）を使った場面転換
- 奥行き（視差、立体的な回転）
- 粒子の集合と拡散
- 数字の数え上げや、線が描かれていく表現

# 合格ライン
- 等速の動きはゼロ。すべての動きに緩急をつける（入りは速く、止まりは柔らかく、ばねの揺れも使う）
- 場面をまたぐ動きは重ねる。前の動きが終わる前に次が始まり、切れ目を感じさせない
- 主要な動きは0.5秒ごとの拍（120BPM相当）にそろえる
- 見せ場の直前に0.3〜0.5秒の「溜め」を置き、強弱を作る
- どの瞬間で一時停止しても、1枚の絵として美しく成立する
- ありがちな表現は避ける（全部フェードイン、虹色の色使い、意味のない回転）

# 最後に
完成したファイルと、絵コンテの表を出してください。
説明は3行以内で十分です。

title: The trick is NOT the prompt. It is one rule: every frame is a pure…
author: yankis0x
prompt:
The trick is NOT the prompt. It is one rule: every frame is a pure function of time.

song -> numpy beat grid -> Opus 5.5 writes one HTML file -> Playwright renders -> ffmpeg blends

step 1 -> pick a royalty-free track around 120 BPM

step 2 -> give Opus 5.5 8 to 12 UI states: button, loader, toggle, chart, command palette

step 3 -> one HTML file, 1440x1440, every style computed inside seek(t). no CSS transitions, no timers

step 4 -> springs as closed-form math, so any frame renders in any order

step 5 -> numpy finds the beats, every UI sound lands on a measured peak

step 6 -> Playwright shoots 4 subframes per frame, ffmpeg tmix blends them into 60fps motion blur

step 7 -> render one frame per beat first, fix what is off the grid, then the full render

the math:

120 BPM x 7 bars = 28 beats = 14 seconds
14 s x 60 fps x 4 subframes = 3,360 browser renders
